title: Unified lightweight endpoint surface for multi-mode inference (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank)
creator: Maya Thompson
summary: Deliver a minimal, unambiguous hosted endpoint surface that consolidates chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank into a small set of interoperable routes with consistent behavior, clear fallbacks, and verified performance & quality targets.
goals: Define a minimal API surface that supports the four primary modes: chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Ensure consistent authentication, rate-limits, and observability across modes
Ship SDK docs and server-side contracts so customers can migrate with minimal code changes
Meet performance SLOs (latency/cost) and quality guardrails validated by automated evals
non_goals: Support for multimodal binary/image inputs in the initial launch
On-prem/private deployment changes (Private product will consume the same surface but has a separate rollout)
Deep per-customer custom model routing or custom VPC network configuration
user_stories: As a frontend engineer, I can call /v1/generate (completions) to get consistent token-streaming behavior and predictable p95 latency so the UI remains snappy
As an ML engineer, I can call /v1/chat with structured messages and function-calling metadata to reproduce conversation state across retries
As a search engineer, I can call /v1/embeddings with a batched payload and receive deterministic vectors within established numeric tolerances
As a ranking engineer, I can call /v1/rerank with a list of candidate IDs and receive a ranked array with stable ordering and explained scores
acceptance_criteria: API contract: endpoints /v1/chat, /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank documented with request/response examples, error codes, and stream semantics
Backward compatibility: existing beta-hosted customers using previous generation endpoints can be routed to the new surface via header toggle with no behavior regression (>99% parity in smoke tests)

Latency SLOs: completions p95 <= 220ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens); chat p95 <= 280ms for 4-turn sessions with caching enabled; embeddings p99 <= 800ms for batched size 64; rerank p95 <= 300ms for candidate set size 20
Throughput: hosted tier sustained throughput validated in a staging load test at 75% of capacity target for 30 minutes without error rate > 0.5%
Quality safety: automated evaluation harness shows no more than 3% degradation in key quality metrics compared to current production baselines
Observability: per-route dashboards created (latency, tokens, cost, errors), and three core alerts in PagerDuty each with runbook links
Documentation: Quickstart guides for each mode, SDK snippets in Python/Node, migration guide, and a small migration checklist published to docs.redwood.ai
Security & compliance: SAML/SSO access gating for console launch ready; security review completed and documented in the ticket thread
E2E tests: CI job that runs end-to-end smoke tests for all four modes against staging and blocks merge on failures
Rollout controls: canary route support by header or customer ID + automated rollback threshold (error rate >1% OR latency SLO breach sustained for 5 minutes)
Cost guardrail: default batching and caching settings applied to hosted default so median token cost is reduced by at least 12% compared to naive per-request execution for the same workload
open_decisions: Default timeout values for long-running generation (30s vs 60s) - tentative default 60s to avoid customer errors; decision required from runtime team
Model tier mapping: which model family is the default for each hosted pricing lane (standard vs premium)
Embeddings vector dimensionality and normalization policy for the hosted default (use 1536 and L2-normalize)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dogfood only - restricted to Redwood employees for 1 week
Stage 1: selected beta customers (25 customers) under a header toggle; monitor P0/P1 metrics for 2 weeks
Stage 2: gradual ramp to 20% of new signups over 72 hours with automatic rollback thresholds configured
Stage 3: full public rollout and deprecation schedule for legacy endpoints (90-day migration window)
launch_checklist: API surface completed and merged: endpoints, schema, streaming semantics
SDK updates committed: Node & Python examples in the monorepo and published to npm/pypi
Confluence PRD and migration guide published with links in the ticket
Performance benchmarking report uploaded (p95/p99, throughput curves) and reviewed by infra
E2E smoke tests green in staging across both default and premium model lanes
Canary routing implemented and verified in staging with automated rollback
Cost dashboard and billing wiring validated with finance
Docs site updated with migration checklist and deprecation notice
Security review signed off and audit artifacts attached
SRE runbooks and oncall playbooks published
SDK release notes published and package versions bumped
Legal and billing hooks validated for migration scenarios
Final stakeholder sign-off meeting scheduled and recorded
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model quality regressions after changing defaults - Mitigation: gated rollout + evaluation harness comparing against held-out prompts
Risk: Latency regressions under bursty load - Mitigation: performance testing with realistic burst profiles and autoscaling playbook validated
Risk: Customer confusion due to endpoint rename consolidation - Mitigation: migration guide, SDK adapters, and header toggle for compatibility
Risk: Increased cost from default batching not tuned - Mitigation: cost monitoring dashboard and conservative default batch sizes; finance sign-off on cost thresholds
notes_and_links: GH: epic PR linking SDK and runtime changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-surface/pull/4132
final_notes: This PRD is intentionally narrow: focus on a small, well-documented surface that reduces customer friction for common workloads. If the open decisions cannot be resolved in the next two cycles, scope the unresolved items into follow-up tickets instead of delaying launch.
